(2024), 'Measuring mind wandering with experience sampling during task performance: An item response theory investigation', Behavior Research Methods 56:7707-7727, doi 10.3758/s13428-024-02446-9, CC BY 4.0, open at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11362314/ (Table 1 and the 'Goller et al. note: STEP 3b -- WHICH INSTRUMENT THE CODES BELONG TO, stated explicitly because the table name points at a secondary source. Zanesco et al. (2024) administered nothing: it is a secondary IRT re-analysis of three existing datasets, so the item codes cannot belong to any Zanesco instrument. They belong to Goller, Banks & Meier (2020)'s SART, and specifically to the SECOND of that study's two paired probes, not the first. Goller's SART carried 36 pairs of probes; probe 1 asked, verbatim, 'What were you just thinking about?' with SIX categorical options (task-related; task-related evaluative positive; task-related evaluative negative; task-unrelated neutral; task-unrelated positive; task-unrelated negative), while probe 2 immediately followed and asked how on- or off-task the participant was on a FIVE-point scale. The live table has 36 items and exactly 5 resp levels, which fits probe 2 and excludes probe 1 (which would give 6); Zanesco et al. say outright 'Only the attentional focus probe (second probe question) was examined herein'. The authors' own name for this measure is 'depth ratings' (manuscript Method; prereg 'Mind wandering depth'), which is what the instrument field records. Not to be confused with the sibling table Zanesco_2023_Zanescoetal2020, whose 28 probes are a DIFFERENT study's 1-6 attentional-focus probe. No established Zanesco convention existed to follow: itemtext/provenance.csv contains no Zanesco row, and neither sibling has been extracted. ITEM_TEXT IS BLANK FOR ALL 36 ITEMS, DELIBERATELY. Every source that describes this probe describes it rather than quoting it: Goller's manuscript reads 'Following these thought probes, subjects were asked about how off or on-task they were on a 5-point Likert scale'; the preregistration reads 'subjects will be asked about how off or on-task they were'; Zanesco et al. (2024) read 'asked how on-task or off-task individuals were according to a five-point scale'. All three are the authors' prose about their procedure, not the string on the screen -- and the contrast is sharp, because the same paragraphs DO quote the first probe verbatim inside quotation marks. Three further routes were tried and none holds the stem: (a) the E-Prime experiment file on OSF ('4 SARTcorrected4blockD - New.ebs2') is an XML wrapper whose entire ScriptContents element is an encrypted 378,080-byte blob -- not base64-of-zlib/gzip/raw-deflate, and containing no printable run longer than 11 characters, so the stimulus text is not readable from it; (b) the E-Prime data export sart1.txt has columns Probe.RESP/Probe.RT and ProbeD.RESP/ProbeD.RT but no stimulus-text column (header read from the first 200 kB by HTTP range request); (c) the published Memory & Cognition version is not open access (Europe PMC: id 32086754, isOpenAccess=N) and the OSF accepted manuscript is the same text. So a stem was NOT invented, per SKILL Step 4's 'do not invent structure'; the picture-stimulus ruling of 2026-09-05 is the closest precedent -- ship what the source really published (instrument identity and the verbatim anchors) and leave item_text blank. This is NOT the #1770 option-only case the rule bars: there the stems existed one hop away, and here they exist nowhere in the deposit or the paper's supplements, while the anchors themselves carry the item's referent (attentional focus, on-task vs off-task) rather than being a generic agreement scale. Note also that all 36 items are repeated occasions of ONE question, so identical item_text on every row would carry no information the instrument field does not. OPTION_TEXT IS VERBATIM AND ITS NUMBERING IS THE SOURCE'S OWN, which is why mapping_basis=paper_explicit rather than paper_order: Goller's manuscript prints the anchors with the integers attached -- '(1 = Completely on-task, 2 = Mostly on-task, 3 = Both on the task and off-task, 4 = Mostly off-task, 5 = Completely off-task)' -- and those five integers are exactly the live resp set. Capitalisation, hyphenation and the slightly odd 'Both on the task and off-task' are transcribed as printed and not tidied. The prereg's lower-case rendering ('1 = completely on-task, 5 = completely off-task') was not followed; the manuscript is the fuller and later of the two. DERIVATION (core model s3): pattern 1, the code IS the source column name. data/Zanesco_2023.py reads Golleretal2020.csv, drops the id column ('Subject') and any column named exclude/exclusions, and emits item=<column name> for every remaining column, so items T1..T36 are literally the deposit's headers T1..T36 -- nothing positional. The deposit's own analysis script golleretal2020_MIRT.R confirms those headers are the probes in administered order: it takes columns 3:38 as items 1-36, regresses item parameters on time = 0:35, and splits probes 1-18 (early) from 19-36 (later). A verification row and verify_Zanesco_2023_Golleretal2020.R were written anyway because mapping_basis is not data_labels; see verification_Zanesco_2023_Golleretal2020.csv for the numbers. RESPONSE-DATA SCOPE, worth a reader's attention and NOT a defect: the live table has 366 participants while Goller's analysis sample and Zanesco et al.'s Table 1 both report N=355. Golleretal2020.csv has 368 rows, of which 366 carry any probe data and 11 of those are flagged Exclude=1; data/Zanesco_2023.py drops the Exclude column but keeps the rows, so IRW ships the 355 analysed participants plus the 11 the source study excluded. Restricting the live table with the source's own flag reproduces the published mean and SD to three decimals (2.508 / 0.880, N=355), which is how this was established rather than inferred. Missing responses were dropped by the processing script's notna() test, but in fact all 366 retained participants answered all 36 probes (13,176 = 366 x 36, complete cases 366), so there are no coverage gaps and every item carries all five resp levels. RIGHTS: no block. The wording is not a published instrument at all -- it is a single ad hoc thought probe written by Goller, Banks & Meier for their own SART, with no rights holder separate from the authors and no instrument page to carry terms. Nothing resembling a fee, a permission-required route, a non-commercial clause, a no-derivatives clause or a redistribution bar was located for it; itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv holds no SART, thought-probe or mind-wandering row. The words shipped here were taken from the authors' own public OSF node (osf.io/shxb6) and from Zanesco et al. (2024), which is CC BY 4.0. Per the standing rule no 'ship' row was written to the register. LANGUAGE: administered in English (undergraduates at Western Carolina University), so language and the four _translated columns are omitted rather than emitted empty. correct_response is blank throughout -- a self-report attentional-focus rating has no correct answer. section_id is a single trivial Zanesco_2023_Golleretal2020_1 with a blank section_prompt: the 36 probes are occasions of one question with no testlet or passage structure. instructions is blank because no source quotes the instructions either; Goller's Method describes the SART task instructions ('respond quickly to all non-target stimuli and withhold responses to target stimuli') in the authors' prose, which is a description and not administered text. The verbatim first-probe stem 'What were you just thinking about?' was deliberately NOT placed in section_prompt: it did precede each depth rating, but it is a different item with six options, and a reader joining it to this table's resp 1-5 would mis-read the scale.
